land.text: the Sandomierz Province (eastern Lesser Poland, centred on Sandomierz), given to Henry of Sandomierz by Bolesław III's testament

predecessors.note: The page says the duchy 'was formed in 1138 from the territories of the Kingdom of Poland'; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland row ends in 1138.

land.text: the whole Sandomierz province, which Władysław I the Elbow-high 'seized' after Wenceslaus II's death in 1305; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland shape covers Sandomierz from 1305

successors.note: The Sandomierz page says the duchy 'existed until 1320 when it was incorporated into the Kingdom of Poland' (infobox 'Incorporation into Kingdom of Poland: 1320'; its title bar gives 1304-1333). The dossier ends in 1304, the last Cliopatria shape; 1305-1320 is carried by Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland row (see notes).

capitals.name: Sandomierz
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Sandomierz'. The twelve castellanies the page lists include Lublin, Radom and Wiślica.

rulers.name: Władysław II the Exile
rulers.title: regent
rulers.note: The page lists him as regent 1138-1146.

rulers.name: Bolesław IV the Curly
rulers.note: The High Duke held Sandomierz after Henry's death.

rulers.name: Leszek I the White
rulers.note: Helen of Znojmo regent and Konrad I of Masovia co-ruler 1194-1200 (page list); Leszek killed 24 November 1227.

rulers.name: Bolesław V the Chaste
rulers.note: The Bolesław V page has Grzymisława regent from 1228, Henry the Bearded regent from 1231 (confirmed 1233), personal rule from 1239; the Sandomierz list also gives Bolesław I of Masovia 1229-1232, which no other page opened confirms.

rulers.name: Bolesław II of Masovia
rulers.note: Infobox successor of Leszek in Sandomierz.

rulers.name: Władysław I the Elbow-high
rulers.note: First reign; 'in the second half of 1289 ... managed to consolidate his rule in the Duchy of Sandomierz'.

rulers.name: Wenceslaus II of Bohemia
rulers.note: Bohemian troops drove Władysław out of Sandomierz in 1292.

correction.text: The Cliopatria 1139 shape applied one year earlier: Sandomierz Land between the Pilica, Vistula, San and Dunajec

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 1139, the page has the duchy 'formed in 1138' (infobox 'Testament of Bolesław III Wrymouth: 1138'). The page gives no area, so the infobox comparison was not possible; the territory 'centred around Sandomierz Land ... between the rivers of Pilica, Vistula, San, and Dunajec' fits the 1139 shape (bbox 20.2-23.1 E, 49.7-52.0 N).

1139-1146, 30,680 km2 (129 cells; 82% inside the Lesser Poland region). The testament gives 'Henry of Sandomierz: the Sandomierz Province (eastern Lesser Poland, centered on Sandomierz)'; Władysław II held the duchy as regent to 1146 (Sandomierz page). No infobox area on the page. The outline stops about 35 km north of Wiślica (gazetteer check), which the page lists among the duchy's twelve castellanies with Lublin and Radom (both inside the outline); the found event adds Wiślica.

1147-1168, 30,705 km2, same bbox. Henry ruled 1146-1166 and died in 1166 'killed by the Old Prussians'; the page has Wiślica 'split off' in 1166 and reintegrated in 1173, which narrows the duchy for 1166-1172 (ledger events); the Cliopatria outline does not reach Wiślica and the extent of the castellany is not on the page (30 km radius assumed). Bolesław IV the Curly held the duchy 1166-1173 as High Duke; Cliopatria draws Sandomierz inside the Masovia row's big shape from 1169 (see _1169).

correction.text: The Sandomierz Province as in the 1177 shape, ruled by Bolesław IV the Curly (1166-1173) and then Casimir II (1173-)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Sandomierz shape in 1169-1176 (the land lies inside the Duchy of Masovia's 156,017 km2 shape for those years). The page's ruler list has the duchy continuing: Bolesław IV the Curly 1166-1173, then Casimir II 1173-1194 ('Mieszko III gave him the whole duchy after Bolesław IV died in 1173', Casimir II page). The 1177 shape is used. The Masovia dossier should drop Sandomierz from its 1169-1176 shape.

correction.text: Sandomierz plus the Seniorate Province at Kraków (Lesser Poland) from 1177

keyframe_review.note: 1177-1187, 30,630 km2. In 1177 Casimir II 'became ruler of the Polish Seniorate Province at Kraków' besides Sandomierz, and in 1186 'took Masovia proper' when Duke Leszek of Masovia died (ledger events). Cliopatria draws the Seniorate in these years under the Duchy of Greater Poland (116,934 km2, which covers Kraków); the corrected shape adds Lesser Poland (Kraków) from 1177 and the 1186 Masovia gain is a ledger event. Casimir held Kalisz and Gniezno 1177-1182 (succession table) and lost them to Mieszko III in 1181; not drawn.

correction.text: Casimir II's lands: Sandomierz, Kraków and the Seniorate Province, and Masovia proper (from 1186)

keyframe_review.note: 1188-1191, 141,788 km2 (609 cells: Masovia 91%, Lesser Poland 70%, Kuyavia 78%, Pomerelia 63% of those regions). The Casimir II page puts in his hands the Seniorate at Kraków, Sandomierz and Masovia (from 1186) but says that 'Mieszko III occupied the lands of Kuyavia up to the Vistula River' shortly after 1186, and gives no Pomerelia beyond Duke Sambor I as a Polish vassal; the corrected shape is Sandomierz plus Lesser Poland plus Masovia. In 1191 Mieszko III took Wawel and Casimir 'later regained the capital without a fight' (undated). Pomerelia as the Seniorate's vassal (Testament page) is left to the vassal tint.

correction.text: Sandomierz, Kraków and the Seniorate and Masovia as held by Casimir II and, to 1197, by his sons' regency

keyframe_review.note: 1192-1201, 142,236 km2: as 1188. Casimir died on 5 May 1194, 'the succession was split between Leszek the White and Konrad I of Masovia'; Mieszko III regained Kraków in 1198 (Helen of Znojmo's agreement), Leszek held it 'briefly' in 1199 and Mieszko ruled until 13 March 1202; 'ca. 1200 Leszek and Konrad divided their domains. Konrad received Masovia and Kuyavia, and Leszek kept Sandomierz'. The ledger carries those losses, so by 1201 only Sandomierz remains, which is the Cliopatria shape of 1202.

1202-1205, 30,607 km2: Sandomierz alone. Mieszko III died on 13 March 1202; Kraków went to Władysław III Spindleshanks ('invited ... to rule Kraków') and Leszek was recalled 'after Gryfita's death (1202)', with the end of Władysław's reign dated 'autumn 1202 or 1206/1210' by different historians. Cliopatria draws Kraków under the Duchy of Greater Poland in 1202-1205 and the ledger gives Leszek Kraków in 1206, the date the infobox gives.

correction.text: Sandomierz plus Kraków and the Seniorate (Lesser Poland) under High Duke Leszek the White

keyframe_review.note: 1206-1209, 113,238 km2 (477 cells, Masovia 48%, Kuyavia 76%, Pomerelia 63% of those regions). Leszek's infobox reigns as High Duke are '1194-1198, 1199, 1206-1210, 1211-1227'; in 1206 Władysław III was deposed at Kraków (Henry I page). Masovia and Kuyavia were Konrad's since the division of c. 1200 and Masovia has its own Cliopatria shape (35,708 km2) for these years; the corrected shape is Sandomierz plus Lesser Poland (Kraków).

correction.text: Sandomierz plus Kraków and the Seniorate from 1211 (lost to Mieszko Tanglefoot in 1210)

keyframe_review.note: 1210-1215, 30,607 km2 (Sandomierz alone). Mieszko IV Tanglefoot seized Kraków in 1210 after Leszek's excommunication and held it 'about a year' (Henry I page); Leszek's infobox gives 1211-1227 as High Duke, so Kraków is Leszek's again from 1211 and the Cliopatria shape (with the Duchy of Opole's 95,164 km2 shape taking the seniorate until 1215) is wrong for 1211-1215. The ledger removes Kraków in 1210 and restores it in 1211.

correction.text: Sandomierz plus Kraków and the Seniorate under Leszek the White

keyframe_review.note: 1216-1219, 113,281 km2: as 1206. Leszek held Kraków as High Duke through 1227; 1218 alliance with Henry I and Władysław III at Sądowel ('dux totius Poloniae' since 1218); 'in 1218 Leszek lost a small area between the Narew and Bug rivers' (holder and extent not on the page, not drawn). Overshoot of the Cliopatria outline into Masovia, Kuyavia and Pomerelia removed as in 1206.

correction.text: Sandomierz plus Kraków and the Seniorate under Leszek the White

keyframe_review.note: 1220-1226, 113,238 km2: as 1216. A joint expedition with Hungary proclaimed Coloman and Salomea rulers of Galicia at the end of 1219 and the 1221 and 1225 expeditions failed: no border change.

1227-1240, 30,631 km2: Sandomierz proper for the minor Bolesław V (born 21 June 1226). Leszek was killed on 24 November 1227; regency of Grzymisława from 1228, Henry the Bearded 'took over Sandomierz' in 1231 (confirmed regent 1233), Konrad captured the boy in 1233, the Treaty of Luchani (August 1234) 'gave Bolesław Sandomierz', Konrad invaded in 1235 and Bolesław lost the Radom district; Konrad renounced his claim on 9 July 1239 (Radom stays inside the Cliopatria outline throughout; ledger: lost 1235, back 1239). Kraków is outside the duchy in these years (Henry the Bearded governor 1228, High Duke 1232-1238).

correction.text: Sandomierz, with Kraków from 25 May 1243 (Battle of Suchodoły) under Bolesław V the Chaste

keyframe_review.note: 1241-1249, 28,591 km2: Sandomierz proper, trimmed in the north (bbox to 51.92 N instead of 52.05 N); the pages opened do not date or explain the trim. Radom stays inside the outline throughout (ledger: lost 1235, back 1239). Mongols took Lublin and Zawichost in January 1241 and burned Sandomierz on 13 February; Konrad entered Kraków on 10 July 1241 and Bolesław regained it on 25 May 1243 (ledger). From 1243 Kraków belongs to Bolesław V but Cliopatria keeps the seniorate in the Duchy of Silesia's shape until 1249. [Reviewer eu-15-e, 2026-10-25: verdict was ok; the ledger gains Kraków in 1243 ('With this victory, Bolesław the Chaste regained the government over Kraków', Bolesław V page), so the shape is adjusted like the 1250 one.]

correction.text: Sandomierz plus Kraków and Lesser Poland under Bolesław V the Chaste

keyframe_review.note: 1250-1278, 112,894 km2 (477 cells: Masovia 48%, Kuyavia 76%, Pomerelia 63% of those regions). Bolesław V held Sandomierz and, from 25 May 1243, Kraków as High Duke until his death on 7 December 1279; the page records only raids and expeditions into Kujawy (1259), against Opole-Racibórz (1273) and Wrocław (1271), no annexation of Masovia, Kuyavia or Pomerelia. The corrected shape is Sandomierz plus Lesser Poland; the Mongol-Ruthenian devastation of Sandomierz, Lublin and Kraków (November 1259) moved no border.

1279-1284, 30,724 km2: Sandomierz alone. Leszek II 'inherited Kraków and Sandomierz as High Duke' on 7 December 1279; Cliopatria draws Kraków as its own Grand Duchy of Kraków (26,864 km2) from 1279, so the shape drops the seniorate (ledger 'split'). In February 1280 Leo of Galicia 'invaded Lublin ... and besieged Sandomierz'; his army fled after Goźlice on 23 February.

1285-1293, 30,607 km2: Sandomierz alone. Leszek II died on 30 September 1288; Władysław I the Elbow-high consolidated his rule in the duchy in the second half of 1289; in 1292 Bohemian troops drove him out (ledger 'rename'). The Mongols invaded Lesser Poland a third time in 1287-1288 (no change).

1294-1304, 25,670 km2: Sandomierz without 22 cells (about 4,900 km2) in the east, between 22.3 E and 23.0 E from 50.8 N to 51.9 N, which are inside Cliopatria's Galicia-Volhynia shape of 1294 (gazetteer check). Wenceslaus II ruled the duchy 1292-1304; no page opened dates the loss of the eastern Lublin land (page silent, ledger confidence 1). 'In 1304, Lokietek returned, capturing Wislica'.

region.text: the Sandomierz Province (eastern Lesser Poland, centered on Sandomierz), with the Wiślica castellany that the Cliopatria outline leaves out

ledger.note: 1138: Bolesław III's testament takes effect and Henry of Sandomierz receives the Sandomierz Province. 'it would be enacted upon his death in 1138'; 'Henry of Sandomierz: the Sandomierz Province (eastern Lesser Poland, centered on Sandomierz)'. The Sandomierz page: the duchy 'formed in 1138 from the territories of the Kingdom of Poland'; Władysław II ruled it as regent to 1146.

region.text: Wiślica, one of the duchy's twelve castellanies

ledger.note: 1166: Wiślica splits off as Henry dies. Page: '1166: Wiślica split off, and Henry died'; Casimir II page: 'Duke of Wiślica in Lesser Poland from 1166 to 1173'.
1173: Casimir II reunites the province. Page: 'Wiślica was reintegrated, and Casimir II reunited the province'; Casimir II page: Mieszko III 'gave him the whole duchy after Bolesław IV died in 1173'.

region.text: Kraków and the Polish Seniorate Province

ledger.note: 1177: Casimir II takes the Seniorate at Kraków. 'In 1177, he became ruler of the Polish Seniorate Province at Kraków' after a revolt took Kraków from Mieszko III (who ruled it 1173-1177, Leszek the White page). The Seniorate's extent (western Lesser Poland, eastern Greater Poland, western Kuyavia, Wieluń Land) is in the Testament page; only Lesser Poland is drawn.

1186: Casimir II takes Masovia. 'In 1186, Duke Leszek of Masovia died'; Casimir took Masovia proper while Mieszko III 'occupied the lands of Kuyavia up to the Vistula River'. He is listed as Duke of Masovia from 1186.
1195: the war for Kraków begins. 'The war began in 1195'; Mozgawa near Jędrzejów was fought on 13 September 1195. Leszek (a boy of ten) and his regents against Mieszko III the Old.
1198: Mieszko III wins Kraków by agreement. 'In 1198, Mieszko III finally regained power over the Seniorate Province through an agreement with Helen of Znojmo.'
1198: Kraków passes to Mieszko III. See the agreement with Helen of Znojmo, the regent; Casimir II's heirs keep Sandomierz.
1199: Leszek holds Kraków for a short time. 'Leszek briefly held Kraków again, interrupting Mieszko III's control.'
1199: Mieszko III resumes Kraków. The page does not say when; he ruled 'until his death on 13 March 1202'. Date bridged inside 1199-1200.

region.text: Masovia (and Kuyavia, which was never drawn here)

ledger.note: c. 1200: Konrad takes Masovia and Kuyavia. 'Leszek and Konrad divided their domains. Konrad received Masovia and Kuyavia, and Leszek kept Sandomierz' (Sandomierz page: Konrad and the regent Helen to 1200).
1206: Leszek is High Duke at Kraków. Infobox reigns '1206-1210'; Henry I page: 'Władysław III Spindleshanks was deposed at Kraków, and Leszek the White became High Duke'.
1210: Mieszko Tanglefoot seizes Kraków. Leszek was 'excommunicated through a papal bull', letting Mieszko Tanglefoot seize Kraków; Henry I page: Mieszko 'held it for about a year'.
1211: Leszek recovers Kraków. His infobox gives '1211-1227' as High Duke; Mieszko held Kraków about a year.
1214: peace of Spiš gives Leszek Przemyśl and Lubaczów. After the defeat at the Bobrka River 'Coloman was given Galicia-Volhynia, and Leszek gained Przemyśl and Lubaczów'; the page implies the year.
1215: the Hungarians take Przemyśl and Lubaczów back. 'The Hungarians broke the alliance and took Przemyśl and Lubaczów back.'

1227: Leszek is killed and Kraków leaves Sandomierz. He was killed on 24 November 1227 at Marcinkowo after the Gąsawa meeting; the page names no holder of Kraków afterwards (Henry the Bearded is made governor of Kraków at Cienia on 5 May 1228 and High Duke in 1232, Henry I page). Counterpart is Cliopatria's: the Duchy of Greater Poland's shape covers Kraków 1227-1235.
1235: Konrad of Masovia takes the Radom district. In June 1235 'Konrad then invaded Sandomierz, and Bolesław lost the Radom district'.

1239: Konrad gives up on Sandomierz. 'On 9 July, at Przedbórz, Konrad renounced his claims to Sandomierz, and Bolesław began his personal government.' The page does not say that the Radom district came back; Cliopatria keeps Radom inside the Sandomierz outline for 1241-1304, which is the bridge (confidence 1).

1241: Konrad of Masovia enters Kraków while Bolesław V is in exile. 'On 10 July 1241 Konrad entered Kraków'; Bolesław had fled to Hungary and then Moravia after the Mongols burned Sandomierz (13 February).
1243: Bolesław V wins Kraków at Suchodoły. '25 May 1243: At the Battle of Suchodoły, Bolesław's forces defeated Konrad's Masovian troops, and Bolesław regained Kraków.'
1243: Bolesław V becomes High Duke at Kraków. He 'regained Kraków. He was 17 and became High Duke that year.'

1279: Kraków is separated from Sandomierz. Bolesław V died on 7 December 1279; Leszek the Black 'inherited Kraków and Sandomierz as High Duke'. Cliopatria draws Kraków as the Grand Duchy of Kraków from 1279, a separate state in personal union with Sandomierz until 1288.

1292: Wenceslaus II of Bohemia takes Sandomierz. Bohemian troops 'drove Władysław the Short first from Sandomierz' (agreement of 9 October 1292); the Sandomierz page lists Wenceslaus II as ruler 1292-1304 and the Wenceslaus II page lists him as Duke of Cracow 1291-1305. The duchy keeps its outline under the Přemyslid king.

region.text: the eastern strip of the Lublin Land that the 1293 shape holds and the 1294 shape does not

ledger.note: 1294: Cliopatria drops the eastern edge of Sandomierz. The 22 cells lost between 1293 and 1294 lie inside the Galicia-Volhynia shape of 1294; none of the pages opened mentions Lublin Land in these years (Leo I of Galicia page: nothing; the Sandomierz page names Lublin among its twelve castellanies).

1304: Władysław the Elbow-high returns and takes Wiślica. 'In 1304, Lokietek returned, capturing Wislica'; the Elbow-high page: he 'settled in Sandomierz' and 'took the castles at Wiślica and Lelów' (Lelów lies outside the duchy). Counterpart is the Bohemian king who held the duchy. [Reviewer eu-15-e, 2026-10-25: was a gain from kingdom-of-bohemia; the duchy has held Wiślica since 1173 and is Wenceslaus II's after the 1292 rename, so Łokietek's capture of Wiślica in 1304 is a loss of the Bohemian-held duchy.]

1304: last year of the Cliopatria shape; the land passes to Łokietek's Poland. 'After the death of Wenceslaus (1305), he seized the whole province'; 'at the end of 1305 Władysław took the duchies of Sandomierz, Sieradz-Łęczyca and Brześć Kujawski' (Elbow-high page). The page ends the duchy in 1320 ('incorporated into the Kingdom of Poland'); 1304 is Cliopatria's year (its Kingdom of Poland shape starts in 1305).

wars.name: War for the Seniorate (Mozgawa)
wars.outcome: Leszek the White and Konrad of Masovia against Mieszko III the Old, who regained the Seniorate Province by agreement with Helen of Znojmo in 1198 and held it (Leszek briefly in 1199) until 13 March 1202.
wars.note: Battle of Mozgawa near Jędrzejów, 13 September 1195.

wars.name: Battle of Zawichost
wars.outcome: On 14 October 1205 Leszek and Konrad defeated Roman the Great, who was killed; no Polish land changed hands.

wars.name: Leszek's war for Galicia (Bobrka, Spiš)
wars.outcome: After Leszek's defeat at the Bobrka River the peace of Spiš gave him Przemyśl and Lubaczów in 1214; the Hungarians took them back in 1215.
wars.note: 1212 Leszek 'took several border towns' in Volhynia and Galicia; 1213 failed to stop Władysław seizing Galicia.

wars.name: Wars of Bolesław V with Konrad I of Masovia
wars.outcome: Konrad captured Bolesław in 1233 and took the Radom district in 1235; Bolesław won Kraków at Suchodoły on 25 May 1243, lost and retook Lelów in 1246, and Konrad died on 31 August 1247.
wars.note: Treaty of Luchani (August 1234) gave Bolesław Sandomierz; Konrad renounced his claim on 9 July 1239 at Przedbórz.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Poland (1241)
wars.outcome: The Mongols took Lublin and Zawichost in January 1241 and burned Sandomierz on 13 February; Bolesław V fled to Hungary and Moravia. No annexation.

wars.name: Mongol-Ruthenian raid of 1259-1260
wars.outcome: In November 1259 Mongols and Ruthenians destroyed Sandomierz, Lublin and Kraków and left Lesser Poland in February 1260; no annexation.

wars.name: Leo of Galicia's invasion of Lublin and Sandomierz
wars.outcome: Leo invaded Lublin in February 1280, crossed the Vistula and besieged Sandomierz; he fled after the battle of Goźlice on 23 February 1280.
wars.note: Leo I page: 'His attempt to capture Kraków in 1280 ended in failure'.

wars.name: War for the Kraków succession
wars.outcome: After Leszek the Black's death (30 September 1288) Władysław the Elbow-high held Sandomierz from 1289; Bohemian troops drove him out in 1292 and Wenceslaus II ruled Sandomierz and Kraków until 1305.
wars.note: Battle of Siewierz, 26 February 1289; Henry IV Probus died 23 June 1290; 9 October 1292 Władysław and Casimir renounced claims to Lesser Poland.

certainty.note: Sandomierz Land is a duchy of castellanies with no treaty or survey lines on the pages opened; its frontiers with Rus' (the San and Bug) and Masovia are approximate. The Treaty of Luchani (August 1234) and the division of c. 1200 fix who holds the duchy, not its boundary.

notes:
eu-15-e, Duchy of Sandomierz. Start 1138 and the capital follow the page; the dossier ends in 1304 (last Cliopatria shape), but the page says the duchy 'existed until 1320 when it was incorporated into the Kingdom of Poland' (infobox 1320; the title bar says 1304-1333); Cliopatria hands the land to its Kingdom of Poland row from 1305 and the gazetteer confirms that shape covers Sandomierz and Lublin 1305-1334, so 1305-1320 is left to the Kingdom of Poland dossier (an Elbow-high Sandomierz 1305-1320 would double-draw).

How Cliopatria uses this row. Its big shapes (1188-1201, 1206-1209, 1216-1226, 1250-1278; 113-142 thousand km2) are the realm of whoever of the Sandomierz line held Kraków as High Duke, with 63% of Pomerelia, 76% of Kuyavia and much of Masovia thrown in; the small shapes (about 30.6 thousand km2) are Sandomierz Land alone. The pages support Sandomierz plus Kraków/Lesser Poland (and Masovia only 1186-c. 1200), so the big shapes are 'adjust' with Sandomierz + Lesser Poland (+ Masovia). Pomerelia is the Seniorate's fief (Testament page) and is left to the vassal tint, with no dated vassal event on any page (the Casimir II page dates no homage), so none is recorded. The Seniorate in 1177-1187 is drawn by Cliopatria under the Duchy of Greater Poland, in 1202-1205 and 1227-1235 under Greater Poland, in 1210-1215 under Opole, in 1236-1249 under Silesia: the Greater Poland, Opole and Silesia dossiers (eu-15, this batch) should agree on the hand-over years given here.

Disagreements between pages: Wiślica returned in 1173 (Sandomierz and Casimir II pages agree). The Sandomierz ruler list gives Bolesław V 1227-1279, 'Bolesław I of Masovia 1229-1232' and Konrad I with Helen 1194-1200; the Bolesław V page has Grzymisława regent 1228-1231, Henry the Bearded 1231 (confirmed regent 1233), Bolesław 'Duke of Sandomierz in Lesser Poland from 1232', personal government 1239; the Henry II page says Henry II was regent of Sandomierz and Opole-Racibórz in 1238-1239. Leszek's page gives Konrad's share (Masovia and Kuyavia) as c. 1200, the Casimir II page as the succession of 1194. Mozgawa is dated 13 September 1195.
